title: Illuminating the Effects of Dynamic Lighting on Student Learning

findings.antecedent: Focus lighting (6000K-100fc average maintained) during instruction
findings.consequent: Oral Reading Fluency (ORF) performance (words read correctly per minute)
findings.mechanism: focus light setting as an instructional technology improved the reading performance of the experimental group at a rate greater than the improvement experienced by the control group, implying enhanced cognitive capacity (concentration, attention).
findings.source: Results and Discussion, ORF section, Figure 4

stimuli.description: Classrooms equipped with dynamic lighting systems. 'Focus' lighting was 1000 lux at 6500 K. 'Normal' lighting was 500 lux at 3500 K. Lighting fixtures contained three lamps (two cool, one warm) with a diffuser plate, allowing incremental dimming/increasing light output per selected scene.
stimuli.source: Participants, Method, and Instrumentation; Dynamic Lighting in the Classroom; Figures 2 and 3

limitations: Quasi-experimental design where classrooms, not students, were randomly assigned, limiting control for teacher effects.
All students were tested in a normal lighting environment, potentially disadvantaging the focus lighting group due to encoding specificity.
Only one measure was used for each of the three dependent variables, potentially leading to poor measurement for motivation and concentration.
Students and teachers were aware of the study, potentially leading to conformity bias (exerting more or less effort based on perceived desired outcomes).
Novelty of treatment effects could influence results, suggesting future studies should eliminate this by having entire schools use focus lighting for several years.
